criteria: Clears the fraction correctly, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Multiply both sides by 2 to clear the fraction.
$$\begin{aligned} x+\dfrac{x-1}{2} &= 9 \\ 2x+x-1 &= 18 \\ 3x &= 19 \\ x &= \dfrac{19}{3} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Writes the fraction using a common denominator, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Charlotte is thinking of a number. She lets the number be $x$. When Charlotte subtracts 6 from this number and multiplies the result by 4, the answer is 3 more than $x$.

Which equation can be used to find $x$?

solutions.latex:
Translate each phrase into algebra.

"Subtracts 6 from this number" gives $x-6$.

"Multiplies the result by 4" gives $4(x-6)$.

"3 more than $x$" gives $x+3$.

So the equation is
$$4(x-6)=x+3$$
This is option C. Options B and D multiply only $x$ by $4$, not the whole difference.

solutions.latex:
Dividing both sides by 2 gives $3x-1=8$, so the error is in Line 2.

The solution should read:
$$\begin{aligned}2(3x-1)&=16\\3x-1&=8\\3x&=9\\x&=3\end{aligned}$$
Hence option B is correct.
